articles.summary: MUMBAI: In yet another instance of a gangland attack on a film personality, unidentified motorcycle-borne assailants repeatedly fired at a car carrying
articles.body: MUMBAI: In yet another instance of a gangland attack on a film personality, unidentified motorcycle-borne assailants repeatedly fired at a car carrying actor Tiger Shroff and his driver Firdaus in Juhu around 7 pm Sunday, injuring Firdaus on his hand and a fan standing nearby who sustained bullet wounds near his chest.Seven shots were fired in all. The actor who was leaving after attending a birthday party at Pushpa Narsee Park, also known as Jamnabai Nursery, escaped with “minor abrasions” from pieces of shattered glass from the vehicle’s windscreen.Two persons identifying themselves as Anil Pandit and Harman Sandhu, and claiming to be affiliated with the Lawrence Bishnoi gang, took responsibility for the attack in a voice note posted on social media.Amid political reactions questioning the city’s law and order situation, CM Devendra Fadnavis took a briefing from police commissioner Deven Bharti and sought strict action. He also rang Tiger Shroff and assured him saying, “We are all with you.”The incident took place barely 350 metres away from Juhu police station. The vehicle was slowly exiting the venue when two of the assailants, standing amidst a crowd of curious onlookers, sprang in front of the car and opened fire repeatedly. At least one bullet went through the shattered glass of the vehicle. Juhu police said the three assailants, in white shirts, fled in seconds towards SV Road and Vile Parle railway station on a bike kept idling by their accomplice.Also read: ‘Jaldi le kar jaao, Tiger’: Video shows seat switch as Tiger Shroff takes the wheel after attackDespite being injured, Shroff’s driver emerged from the vehicle and tried to chase them. A senior doctor at Nanavati Hospital, where Shroff and Firdaus were taken, said initial scans showed a foreign body lodged in the latter’s left hand as a result of a bullet injury. He is likely to undergo surgery.In a purported video going viral on social media, one of the two shooters appears unable to fire when he is closest to the car window. The gun seemingly jams as he prepares to fire a sixth shot at point-blank range.Tiger attack: 15 teams tracing shootersPolice were registering an FIR and seeking details from actor Tiger Shroff about any recent threat calls or warnings after unidentified motorcycle-borne assailants repeatedly fired at his car on Sunday. Fifteen teams have been formed to trace the assailants. Juhu police and Mumbai crime branch officers were examining CCTV footage to identify them and establish their escape route.Also Read: ‘Should focus on actual criminals’: Dipke jabs police after shots fired at Tiger Shroff“Shroff only has minor abrasions,” said a senior doctor at Nanavati Hospital. The actor was in the hospital’s emergency room till the time of going to the press, awaiting doctor’s advice on his discharge and the treatment plan for his driver.The third person injured in the firing—a passerby identified by police as 35-year-old Umesh Charan—sustained bullet injuries on the right side of his chest, according to Dr Chhaya Shinde, dean of BMC-run Cooper Hospital in Juhu. “He is stable at the moment but will need immediate surgery,” said a doctor.In a press release, BMC said the third patient arrived at the Cooper Hospital casualty at 7.10pm with a “history of a gunshot wound sustained at 6.30pm at Vile Parle West while covering a football match featuring Tiger Shroff. “The patient came with an entry wound at 2cm below left nipple,” the release added.Also Read: ‘Jaldi le kar jaao, Tiger’: Video shows actor taking wheel after attackPolice initially said Shroff suffered slight abrasions from glass fragments after the car’s windows shattered, but DCP (west zone 2) Mohit Garg said the actor was not injured.Meanwhile, the Lawrence Bishnoi gang claimed responsibility on social media for the attack. The gang claimed Shroff had been targeted as he ignored their warnings and they also threatened to target anyone who works with superstar Salman Khan.Sources said that Shroff had been being tracked by the shooters for a few days.Posted by Lawrence’s aide, Anil Pandit, the message explicitly stated that Pandit and Harman Sandhu took full responsibility for the action taken against the actor. According to the post, the individuals involved had previously contacted the actor with warnings that were allegedly ignored, leading to the latest targeted event.The statement went on to issue a broad warning to members of the Mumbai film industry, threatening that anyone who fails to listen to them or continues to work with Salman Khan will be targeted next. The message concluded with threats directed at rival gang members and was accompanied by several hashtags referencing the Lawrence Bishnoi group and other affiliated associate networks. Police are verifying the social media post and a voice note.Pandit had earlier claimed responsibility for a shooting outside singer Guru Randhawa’s Delhi gym over an alleged Salman Khan connection.The incident evoked alarm within the film and political circles given the previous fatal attack on politician Baba Siddique in Bandra and the incidence of firing at Salman Khan’s Galaxy Apartment in Bandra Bandstand in 2024.Siddique’s son Zeeshan expressed shock and horror at Sunday’s attack on Tiger Shroff, while NCP (SP) leader Supriya Sule echoed his fears over the worsening law and order situation in the state.You Can Also Check: Gold Rate in Mumbai | Silver Rate in Mumbai | Bank Holidays in Mumbai | Public Holidays in Mumbai | Mumbai AQI | Weather in Mumbai | Petrol Price in Mumbai | Diesel Price in Mumbai | CNG Price in Mumbai | LPG Price in MumbaiStay updated with the latest Mumbai news. articles.body: MUMBAI: Actor Tiger Shroff escaped a firing attack on his car near Juhu police station on Sunday evening after unidentified assailants opened fire as he was leaving a birthday party at Pushpa Narsee Park, also known as Jamnabai Nursery.His driver, Firdaus, sustained a bullet injury to his left hand, while a passerby was also injured in the firing. Despite being hurt, the driver emerged from the vehicle and tried to chase the assailants as they fled.The firing took place around 7pm, barely 350 metres from Juhu police station. According to police, the vehicle was slowly exiting the venue when two assailants, standing amid a crowd of onlookers, stepped in front of the car and opened fire repeatedly.Seven rounds were reportedly fired. At least one bullet pierced the shattered glass of the vehicle's window.The three assailants, reportedly dressed in white shirts, fled towards SV Road and Vile Parle railway station on a motorcycle allegedly kept ready by an accomplice.A video of the incident circulating on social media appears to show one of the shooters struggling to fire when he approaches the car window at close range.Shroff was initially taken to Nanavati Hospital along with his driver. A senior doctor said the actor had suffered minor abrasions from glass fragments, while Firdaus had a foreign body lodged in his left hand following the bullet injury and was likely to require surgery. Deputy Commissioner of Police Mohit Garg later said Shroff had not sustained any gunshot injuries.A third person, identified by police as 35-year-old Umesh Charan, was also injured. According to Dr Chhaya Shinde, dean of BMC-run Cooper Hospital in Juhu, he sustained a bullet wound on the right side of his chest. He was stable but required immediate surgery, a doctor said. A BMC press release stated that he was brought to the hospital's casualty department at 7.10pm with a gunshot wound sustained around 6.30pm in Vile Parle West while covering a football match featuring Shroff.Lawrence gang claims responsibility, threatens Salman Khan's associatesThe Lawrence Bishnoi gang claimed responsibility for the attack in a social media post and voice note, though police said they were verifying the authenticity of the material. The post, attributed to Bishnoi aide Anil Pandit, named Pandit and Harman Sandhu as those taking responsibility for the attack.The message claimed Shroff had ignored warnings not to work with actor Salman Khan and threatened to target others in the film industry who continued to work with Khan. It also contained threats directed at rival gang members.Sources said the shooters had allegedly been tracking Shroff for several days. Police were seeking details from the actor about any recent threat calls or warnings as part of the investigation.Pandit had earlier claimed responsibility for a shooting outside singer Guru Randhawa's gym in Delhi, allegedly linked to Salman Khan. The latest incident has renewed concerns over threats to members of the film industry, following the 2024 firing outside Khan's Galaxy Apartments in Bandra and the fatal shooting of former Maharashtra minister Baba Siddique in October that year.Juhu police and the Mumbai Crime Branch were examining CCTV footage to identify the assailants and establish their escape route. Fifteen teams were formed to track them down, while a forensic team inspected the scene and the vehicle to collect ballistic evidence and determine the exact number of rounds fired.Fadnavis assures actor of support; opposition questions law and orderChief minister Devendra Fadnavis, who also holds the home portfolio, sought details from Mumbai Police Commissioner Deven Bharti and directed the police to expedite the investigation and take strict action against those responsible. He also spoke to Shroff over the phone and assured him that the accused would be traced soon.Deputy chief minister Eknath Shinde visited Shroff's residence late on Sunday to enquire about his well-being. Photographs from the meeting showed the actor with dressings on his shoulder and chest and a bandage on his right arm. Shinde said Shroff had sustained injuries to his hand from gunpowder and glass fragments and assured the family of the government's support.Shinde condemned the firing and said the security of celebrities would be reviewed. He said the government would not tolerate threats or allow gangs to intimidate people.The attack drew criticism from opposition leaders, who questioned the state's law and order situation. Mumbai Congress president Varsha Gaikwad called for a separate home minister, arguing that the chief minister was handling too many portfolios. NCP (SP) MP Supriya Sule questioned the progress of the investigation into Siddique's murder and asked why concerns over security remained unresolved.NCP (SP) MLA Rohit Pawar also raised concerns about recent incidents of violence, including the firing outside filmmaker Rohit Shetty's residence, saying such incidents in Mumbai could affect investor confidence. Other opposition leaders accused the government of failing to curb criminal activity and demanded stronger action against the Bishnoi gang.Siddique's son Zeeshan, who has previously raised concerns about threats to his own security, expressed shock over the attack. He reportedly left the spot after the assault and did not approach the police, the official said.The video purportedly shows the group stripping and assaulting the man before pouring petrol on his private parts. articles.title: A 52-year-old Oregon farmer started building miniature castles from rocks cleared off his land in 1935, turning a winter hobby into a four-acre garden of stone bridges, churches and landmarks
articles.summary: In central Oregon, a collection of ordinary stones became the raw material for an unusual roadside attraction.
articles.body: In central Oregon, a collection of ordinary stones became the raw material for an unusual roadside attraction. Rasmus Petersen, a Danish immigrant who had spent much of his life farming near Redmond, started arranging rocks into miniature buildings during the winter of 1935, according to Petersen Rock Garden, Museum and Peacock Sanctuary. He was 52, and what began as a seasonal pastime gradually spread across the land around his home. Small castles, churches, bridges and other structures took shape from stones gathered in the surrounding region, with ponds and planted areas added to the setting. The result became Petersen Rock Garden, a four-acre site that drew thousands of visitors during its early years and remains a recognised part of the area's history.How Danish immigrant began building Petersen Rock Garden at age 52Petersen arrived in Oregon in 1905, settling first in Junction City before claiming an 80-acre homestead near Redmond the following year. The land was acquired under the Desert Land Act, a federal scheme intended to encourage settlement and irrigation in arid parts of the American West. Farming became his livelihood, and by the 1920s he had expanded his agricultural holdings to 256 acres, growing hay and grain and keeping livestock.The Great Depression brought difficult conditions for farmers across the country. Petersen adapted by turning to potatoes, but it was away from the demands of agricultural work that he began developing a different kind of project. Reportedly, in 1935, at the age of 52, he started using the colder months to build small structures from rocks cleared from his land. What he made with them would eventually draw attention well beyond his immediate neighbours.The stonework that put Petersen Rock Garden on the mapThe stones were not simply building material. Petersen incorporated local agate, jasper, obsidian and other varieties into his miniature constructions, selecting pieces for their shapes, colours and textures. Bridges linked sections of the garden, while castles, churches and monuments gave the site the appearance of a small settlement assembled from the geology of the region.The work grew over time. Water features, fountains, mosses and flowers became part of the surroundings, adding living elements to the carefully arranged stonework. Petersen also collected stones from within roughly 85 miles of his home, according to the garden's historical account. That broad geographical reach meant the site reflected the variety of material found across central Oregon rather than relying entirely on rocks from a single field.Visitors began arriving while the garden was still developing. By 1938, the attraction had reportedly welcomed more than 7,000 people. What had started as something to occupy the winter months was becoming a destination in its own right.The miniature landmarks attract visitorsPetersen Rock Garden eventually covered four acres, with its stone creations arranged among landscaped areas and water. Its appeal lay partly in the contrast between the scale of the structures and the work required to assemble them. Buildings and bridges were made from individual stones, placed together to suggest larger architectural forms in miniature.The site also expanded beyond the garden itself. Historical accounts describe a museum, a diner and a pond with islands among its features. Reportedly, by the early 1950s, annual attendance was said to have reached around 120,000 visitors, placing the garden among the roadside attractions that drew travellers exploring Oregon.One plaque on the property sits beneath a miniature Statue of Liberty. It carries the inscription, “Enjoy yourself. It is later than you think.” The wording offers a small glimpse into the garden's character, although its buildings and collections remain the more substantial record of Petersen's years of work.New owners took steps to restore the historic garden and museumPetersen devoted himself to the project until his death in 1952. His wife, Nyleta Harris, whom he had married in 1950, continued managing the property until she died in 1987. The garden then passed into the care of her daughter, Adele Hegardt, and her husband, Harry. Following Adele's death, her daughter Susan Caward took on responsibility for the site.The stone structures, planted areas and water features all formed part of a landscape that had developed over decades, rather than a conventional museum collection that could be preserved indoors. In 2010, an Oregon family purchased the site, with preservation efforts organised through a nonprofit established to support the garden, museum and peacock sanctuary. The aim was to protect the attraction and restore features associated with its earlier years. A museum refurbishment followed in 2022 after a grant secured through local business Webfoot Home Improvements.A historic attraction enters a new chapterMore recent efforts have focused on bringing people back into the work of caring for the garden. Since 2022, Marci Wayman has been associated with new ownership and plans to develop the landmark as a community-stewarded nonprofit. Volunteers have helped with restoration and upkeep, while organisers have sought wider participation in deciding how the property should be preserved and used.The garden's future now depends on more than the stonework Petersen left behind. Its museum, landscape and other features need attention if they are to remain accessible, and community involvement has become part of that process. The original structures still connect the site to the farmer who began building them in 1935, long before the garden became a familiar stop for visitors travelling through central Oregon.You use AI every day. articles.title: Trump excoriates Zelensky after Ukraine defies US president with major attack on Russia
articles.summary: Ukraine launched one of its biggest drone attacks this year on Russia overnight on Saturday, hitting a key oil terminal in defiance of US President Donald Tr...
articles.body:
Ukraine launched one of its biggest drone attacks this year on Russia overnight on Saturday, hitting a key oil terminal in defiance of US President Donald Trump's demand it stop hitting Russian energy infrastructure.

There have been growing tensions between Ukraine and the US in recent days, prompting fears in Kyiv it could lose essential support as it approaches another winter under relentless Russian attack.

Trump on Friday invoked a waiver exempting Russia from sweeping economic penalties mandated by the US Congress. President Volodymyr Zelensky later told NBC News' "Meet the Press" the US siding with Russia would be a "historic mistake."

Trump said in a Truth Social post on Sunday that he doesn't want to do anything that will drive Russia away from negotiations to end the war in Ukraine, adding that he believes "great progress is being made."

At the same time, he excoriated Zelensky, saying that he "doesn't want to end this war, and probably never did."

"I am in the process of negotiating Peace in the war between Russia and Ukraine, and don't want to do anything that will drive, foolishly, Russia away from the bargaining table," Trump wrote.

Despite this, the Ukrainian president said he spoke to US envoy, Steve Witkoff and Trump's son-in-law Jared Kushner on Sunday as part of "nonstop communication" to work towards to goal of peace.

"We are doing everything on our part to make this happen, and to ensure that America's position is strong and helps bring peace closer," Zelensky posted on X .

But Ukraine is keeping up long-range strikes into Russia. Russia's defense ministry said it shot down 1,015 Ukrainian drones overnight into Sunday over various parts of the country.

One target was the St. Petersburg Oil Terminal, according to Russian authorities. The terminal can handle up to 12.5 million tons per year. Ukraine's Fire Point company, which makes the drones used in the attack, said there was a fire on the terminal's grounds following the strike.

A logistics centers in St. Petersburg was also attacked, according to Ozon, a Russian distribution company, as well as a data center for the Russian VKontakte social media platform.

One person was killed and five wounded in the attacks, with residential homes damaged as well, according to local authorities.

"They shot one down right above us: there was one bright flash, and it shook us up quite strongly," a 41-year old resident of St. Petersburg told CNN.

"I heard a roar, got everyone out of their beds, took the cat, and we hid in the bathroom," another said.

Ukraine's strikes come amid Zelensky's deteriorating relationship with Trump, who last week called Kyiv's strikes on Russian oil refineries a "disgrace."

A week ago, Trump said Russia and Ukraine had agreed to stop attacking each other's energy infrastructure, as the White House tries to relieve pressure on oil and diesel prices ahead of crucial midterm elections.

Neither Kyiv nor Moscow acknowledged such an agreement. Ukraine briefly halted such attacks, but has since resumed them — while Russia never stopped pounding Ukraine's energy plants and cities.

Eleven people were killed and nearly 50 injured across Ukraine in Russian missile and drone attacks in the 24 hours to Sunday morning, according to Ukrainian authorities, including what they called a massive attack on energy facilities in the Odesa region.

"Since the American President announced the energy ceasefire a week ​ago, Russia has ​deliberately ‌attacked ​Ukraine's energy and oil and gas sectors ⁠76 times," Zelensky ​wrote on X Sunday.

Trump has waived sanctions on imports of Russian diesel and on Friday invoked a waiver exempting Russia from sweeping economic penalties mandated by the US Congress, sparking criticism even from Republicans .

In an interview Sunday with "Meet the Press," Zelensky said the waiver strengthened Putin's war against Ukraine while Moscow was failing on the battlefield. He said it was "more support for Russian aggression."

Zelensky also repeated that the Ukrainian military's access to the Starlink system to guide its short-range and battlefield drones was still curtailed.

"It was a message from the American government" to limit the speed at which Ukrainian drones could fly, Zelensky said.

The Trump administration has denied it ordered the service restricted.

Zelensky said that intelligence sharing had been blocked by the US side for three days during ballistic missile attacks but had since been restored. US satellite networks have been critical in providing the Ukrainian military with warnings of incoming missiles.

A Ukrainian source told CNN there was no early warning before a ballistic missile attack on Kyiv on Sunday. This is the third time in a week there has not been an early warning.

Zelensky was also asked about Trump's comments that he was more difficult to deal with than Russian President Vladimir Putin and replied it was "better to have partners who are very open and clear than to have those who are killers, even with a smile on their face."

Zelensky said he wanted to trust Trump and hoped he would change his attitude to Putin.

Asked if Trump was an ally of Ukraine, Zelensky said: "I hope so."

Daria Tarasova, Julia Benbrook and Jennifer Hanlser contributed to this report.

articles.summary: Iranian foreign minister Abbas Araghchi has issued a sharp warning to US President Donald Trump over his threat to “finish the job” against Tehran, saying
articles.body: Iranian foreign minister Abbas Araghchi has issued a sharp warning to US President Donald Trump over his threat to “finish the job” against Tehran, saying Iran came out stronger from the previous confrontation.“Last time you wanted to ‘finish the job’, Iran emerged even stronger. Want to try your luck again? Be our guest. But be careful, we have unfinished jobs too,” Araghchi wrote on X.Taking aim at Netanyahu, the Iranian minister alleged that the Israeli leader was trying to pull the United States into another military conflict to avoid facing legal consequences at home. He cautioned that the fallout could affect both Israel and Trump.“Netanyahu is driving America into another war to stay out of jail, whatever the consequences for Israel—let alone POTUS,” Araghchi said.Trump throws weight behind NetanyahuThe exchange followed Trump's public endorsement of Netanyahu ahead of Israel's October 27 parliamentary election. The US president praised the Israeli leader's handling of the confrontation with Iran and his role in pursuing peace.In a lengthy post on Truth Social addressed to the “Great People of Israel”, Trump called Netanyahu a “Great Warrior Prime Minister” and announced his “Complete and Total Endorsement” of his re-election campaign.Also Read: Putin proposes trilateral summit with Trump, Xi to discuss Ukraine war: ReportTrump also warned Israeli voters against choosing a different leader, suggesting that the United States might have to intervene if they picked the “wrong Leader”.“I am not inclined to do so,” he added.Trump has accused Iran of posing a threat to both Israel and the United States for decades, pointing to slogans such as “Death to Israel, Death to America”. He warned that Tehran could eventually act on those threats.Claiming that Iran had suffered significant military and financial setbacks, Trump said Washington would “soon finish the job” unless the country changed course quickly.You use AI every day. articles.title: World’s oldest shipwreck discovered off Turkey with nearly 4,700-year-old pottery revealing clues to ancient Mediterranean trade
articles.summary: Archaeologists have discovered the world’s oldest known shipwreck off the coast of Kekova Island in Antalya, Turkey.
articles.body: Archaeologists have discovered the world’s oldest known shipwreck off the coast of Kekova Island in Antalya, Turkey. The Early Bronze Age vessel dates back 4,400 to 4,700 years and was around 10 metres long, carrying more than 30 ceramic storage pots, known as amphorae, across the Mediterranean Sea.According to the BBC, the ship’s wooden structure has not survived; its cargo remains scattered across an underwater slope about 30 metres below the surface. Remarkably, some of the pots still contain traces of their original contents, giving researchers a chance to investigate the goods traded in the ancient world.4,700-year-old shipwreck was found with more than 30 ceramic pots in TurkeyThe wreck lies close to Kekova Island in Antalya, southern Turkey, with its artefacts scattered across an underwater slope about 30 metres beneath the waves. Archaeologists estimate that the vessel was around 10 metres long and used to transport goods across the Mediterranean Sea.The expedition, led by Professor Hakan Öniz of Akdeniz University, working with the Mediterranean Archaeology Association, recovered more than 30 ceramic storage pots and three large stone anchors. Ships carried spare anchors on long voyages, according to the expedition’s findings.The wooden structure has not survived, leaving the cargo as the principal evidence of the vessel. The discovery is now considered the world’s oldest known shipwreck, surpassing a wreck found near Dokos in southern Greece.How did archaeologists determine the age of the ancient shipwreckThe ship’s wooden structure has not survived, so archaeologists could not use radiocarbon dating to determine its age. Instead, they examined the shape and decoration of the ceramic pots, as pottery styles are associated with specific historical periods.The amphorae recovered from Kekova have two handles, a ridge around the middle, and a flat base. According to Öniz, their design matches pottery found in Egypt and the Middle East that dates back 4,400 to 4,700 years.The team also compared the pots’ decoration techniques to establish the wreck’s age. These features confirmed that the vessel dates to the Early Bronze Age, a period that coincided with the construction of the Great Pyramid in Egypt.What did archaeologists find inside the ancient shipwreck’s storage potsSome of the recovered amphorae remained intact and contained a thick, glossy residue despite spending thousands of years underwater. Dr Karin Sowada, an archaeologist from Macquarie University in Australia, examined the pots after they were brought to the surface and was surprised by how much material remained inside.Researchers are now analysing the residue to identify what the vessel carried. Possible contents include olive oil, wine or tree resins, although its exact composition has not yet been established. Sowada also suggested that the residue could have come from the reuse of the jars. Given their size, the vessels may have been emptied upon arrival and used again over many years.What does the ancient shipwreck reveal about early Mediterranean tradeArchaeologists believe the vessel began its voyage somewhere along the eastern Mediterranean coast. Its intended destination may have been the ancient city of Troy, in what is now northwestern Turkey, or the Minoan people in Crete.The journey would have involved risks. Strong currents and winds around Kekova Island have caused many shipwrecks, and the surrounding waters contain hundreds of wreck sites. Öniz said his thoughts turned to the people connected with the vessel, including the sailors, the pot makers and those who carried the heavy jars aboard.You use AI every day. articles.title: An 18-year-old built an AI traffic system that changes pedestrian signals based on how safe people feel crossing a road
articles.summary: An 18-year-old student has developed an AI-powered traffic system designed to make road crossings safer for people who need more time to reach the other
articles.body: An 18-year-old student has developed an AI-powered traffic system designed to make road crossings safer for people who need more time to reach the other side. The system is called SmartBlink and instead of a set time for crossing, it changes the pedestrian light timings based on how fast people cross the road. The invention, developed by Phillips Academy student Jay Jung of Massachusetts, aims to make streets more accessible to older adults and others with physical difficulties. His work has also earned recognition at an international science competition.How does the 18-year-old's AI traffic system make pedestrian crossings saferTraditional pedestrian signals give people a limited amount of time to cross a road. While this arrangement may work for many pedestrians, it can leave older adults and people with mobility difficulties struggling to reach the pavement before the signal changes.For Jung, this was not simply a technical problem but something he had noticed during everyday life. His experience walking with his grandparents led him to explore how traffic signals might better serve people moving at various speeds, NiceNews reported.His invention, SmartBlink, uses AI to monitor pedestrian movement and adjust crossing times accordingly. Instead of expecting everyone to cross at the same pace, the system takes account of how long the slower-moving pedestrian may need.The project reflects a different approach to road safety, placing greater emphasis on the people using a crossing instead of treating every pedestrian as though they have identical physical abilities.The idea began with a problem involving his grandparentsJung grew up with his grandparents in South Korea. During his childhood, he noticed that they sometimes struggled to cross streets in Seoul before pedestrian signals changed.Walking with his grandparents to places such as the local grocery shop and park helped him recognise the limitations of conventional crossing signals. The time allowed to cross did not always match the pace at which they could comfortably walk.That experience stayed with him, and eventually influenced how he approached technology. He began to wonder if a more responsive system might be a practical solution. His project exemplifies how a simple observation can lead to an idea that goes beyond the original problem.SmartBlink adjusts crossing time for speed of walkingThe main advantage of SmartBlink is its capacity to estimate the time a pedestrian needs to cross the road. Instead of following an unchanging schedule, the system can adapt the crossing period to the person's observed movement.If a pedestrian signal normally provides 20 seconds to cross, but the system estimates that a person needs 34 seconds, it can add another 14 seconds to the crossing period.This adjustment is intended to reduce the pressure pedestrians may feel when trying to reach the other side before the light changes. It also recognises that crossing a road can be more challenging for someone who walks slowly or uses a mobility aid.According to NiceNews, SmartBlink can identify pedestrians using wheelchairs, crutches or walking canes. Its algorithm has also been adapted to function under different lighting conditions, supporting its potential use during both daytime and night-time hours.A crossing that works well for one person may not provide enough time for another. SmartBlink seeks to address that difference by adapting the signal to the person crossing.The student received international recognition for his inventionJung's work received recognition at the 2026 Regeneron International Science and Engineering Fair, an international competition for secondary-school students presenting scientific and engineering projects.According to the Society for Science, Jung won 1st place in the Behavioral and Social Sciences category for SmartBlink. The project was recognised under the title ‘SmartBlink: Real-Time AI-Driven Adaptive Pedestrian Traffic System for Enhancing Perceived Pedestrian Safety and Traffic Efficiency.’The award came with a prize of $6,000. The recognition placed his project among a broad range of student-led research initiatives exploring practical problems through science and technology. In Jung's case, the focus was on making existing urban infrastructure more responsive to the people who depend on it.Despite the award, the system has not yet been installed at pedestrian crossings. Its next stage involves exploring how it could be tested in actual communities and adapted to local conditions.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.

articles.title: A San Francisco couple built a Buddhist meditation sanctuary in their backyard, but a planning complaint put it at risk
articles.summary: A San Francisco couple is fighting to save their Buddhist meditation sanctuary after an anonymous planning complaint raised concerns about violations of
articles.body: A San Francisco couple is fighting to save their Buddhist meditation sanctuary after an anonymous planning complaint raised concerns about violations of city building rules. Sam Geffner and Mar Rodin built the backyard retreat in their Noe Valley home, completing construction around 2008. The structure, inspired by traditional Japanese architecture, features a meditation room, skylights and deep roof eaves. After using the space for more than a decade, the couple faced the prospect of demolishing it or altering its design. Having spent nearly $30,000 on architects and lawyers, they are now hoping a proposed change to city planning rules will save their sanctuary.Why did a San Francisco couple’s meditation sanctuary face a complaintAccording to the San Francisco Chronicle, the sanctuary stands behind the couple’s rainbow-painted house on Clipper Street in San Francisco. Gently curving stone steps lead to a meditation room built into the sloping hillside, with two skylights allowing natural light into the space. Sliding glass doors open towards a rocky grotto where koi fish swim.The building’s design draws on traditional Japanese architecture, featuring timber framing, a high roof and wide eaves. Geffner has meditated there for nearly 20 years and described its purpose to the San Francisco Chronicle, saying, “It’s a space that separates you from the everyday world.” The couple regard the structure as a refuge connected to their Buddhist meditation practice.Geffner and Rodin began considering a redesign of their backyard around 25 years ago. They hired landscape designer Kent Gordon England, who designed the meditation room and koi pond. According to Geffner, England assured them that they did not need to worry about obtaining permits for such a small addition.Construction was completed around 2008, and the couple used the space for more than a decade without encountering problems. That changed in 2019, when an anonymous complaint was made to San Francisco’s Planning Department alleging that the structure violated city rules. Geffner described the experience as “a rude awakening”, while Rodin said, “We were really trusting in our cowboy.” England did not respond to the newspaper’s request for comment.Why did San Francisco’s meditation sanctuary violate planning rulesSan Francisco’s planning code regulates the size and design of backyard buildings. The rules are intended to preserve open spaces within city blocks and protect natural light and ventilation for neighbouring properties. The couple’s architect acknowledged at the hearing that the room exceeds the height and floor-area requirements.One of the central issues is the building’s roof overhang. The planning code permits a maximum roof overhang of 12 inches, whereas the sanctuary has eaves extending four feet beyond its walls. Those deep eaves are an important feature of the building’s traditional architectural design and part of the couple’s argument for retaining it.After years of uncertainty, Geffner and Rodin appealed to the city’s zoning administrator for an exemption in the summer of 2026. At a hearing, an architect representing the couple argued that an exception should be considered because the structure is built into a hillside and is used as part of their Buddhist faith.Explaining the significance of the design, Geffner told the hearing, “In Buddhist tradition, the peaked roofs and deep eaves are understood as this building’s primary way of signalling this is a sacred, protected space.” The couple also sought support from their neighbours, going door to door and distributing a 13-page packet of photographs documenting the backyard and meditation room. Geffner said they received more than 30 letters of support.How could new zoning rules protect San Francisco’s backyard sanctuaryThe dispute has attracted the attention of Rafael Mandelman, the supervisor representing the district that includes Noe Valley. At a meeting of San Francisco’s Board of Supervisors in September 2026, he introduced a proposed change to the planning code that would allow backyard structures built before 2010 to remain, provided they fell within the scope of the proposed measure.The proposal would extend an existing provision that grandfathered in backyard buildings constructed before 2003. If approved, the revised cut-off date would cover the couple’s sanctuary, which was completed around 2008. Mandelman said the length of time a structure had existed without causing a problem should be considered when deciding whether it needed to be removed.“You look at it and think, ‘That can’t be right,’” Mandelman said of the couple’s predicament, according to the San Francisco Chronicle. He added that it should not be necessary for homeowners to spend years and substantial sums of money trying to secure permission to keep such a structure. The newspaper reported that the number of backyard buildings that could qualify under the proposed change was not yet clear.Patrick Hannan, a spokesperson for San Francisco’s recently merged planning and building inspection departments, said planning staff had worked with Mandelman on the proposal. In a statement quoted by the newspaper, Hannan said, “Our job is to balance priorities when they conflict in the real world.” He described the proposed amendment as “a targeted way to let the small meditation space stay while ensuring that the interior-block open space will be preserved.”What happens next in the backyard sanctuary zoning disputeThe zoning administrator, Corey Teague, told the couple at the hearing that he would consider their arguments and respond later. According to Hannan, Teague has remained in regular contact with the couple’s architect, although Geffner and Rodin had not received a final decision at the time of the San Francisco Chronicle report.Mandelman’s proposed ordinance is expected to go before the full Board of Supervisors in the coming months. If it passes, it would supersede the zoning administrator’s determination on the matter. If it does not pass, the couple could still receive an exemption from the zoning administrator. They would also have the option to appeal an unfavourable decision, although that process would probably increase their costs.Why are San Francisco residents struggling with building permitsThe case comes amid wider difficulties faced by San Francisco residents navigating the city’s planning and building regulations. The San Francisco Chronicle reported that even Supervisor Myrna Melgar, a former president of the San Francisco Planning Commission, had previously described struggling to establish whether she needed a permit to replace a backyard gazebo.For now, Geffner and Rodin intend to continue using the meditation room while they await the outcome of the planning process. The sanctuary has remained part of their lives for decades, and its future depends on the outcome of the proposed code change or the decision on their exemption request. Reflecting on the role meditation plays in dealing with uncertainty, Geffner told the San Francisco Chronicle, “Meditation is a way of bringing a little control over what’s out of control. Reminding you not to take it too seriously.”You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.

articles.title: IMD launches WebGIS-based decision support system to improve cyclone disaster preparedness
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: As an additional disaster preparedness tool to support ground-level action ahead of cyclones, India meteorological department (IMD) has
articles.body: NEW DELHI: As an additional disaster preparedness tool to support ground-level action ahead of cyclones, India meteorological department (IMD) has launched an interactive WebGIS-based platform that will serve as a decision support system (DSS), bringing critical cyclone warnings and marine weather information together in one place.The system will help users, including disaster management authorities, govt agencies and the general public, better understand potential hazards and their likely impacts. It aims to bridge the gap between weather forecasts and their practical application, enabling better preparedness, timely action and enhanced public safety during cyclones and other severe weather events.The launch took place during the bi-annual pre-cyclone exercise meeting for the post-monsoon season (Oct-Dec) under the chairmanship of Mrutyunjay Mohapatra, director general of meteorology, IMD, last week. The DSS platform for the public isavailable on the websites of IMD and regional specialised meteorological centre (RSMC).“Through interactive maps and visualisations of cyclone tracks, intensity, winds, rainfall, storm surge and rainfall forecasts for river catchments, the platform helps users access relevant information and make informed decisions,” said the ministry of earth sciences (MoES) in a statement.IMD has taken a number of steps in recent years to continuously enhance the capabilities in monitoring, numerical modelling and forecasting of the hazards associated with cyclones, and demonstrated its capability to provide early warning for cyclones with high precision. It has, over the years, emerged as the best in the world for the accuracy of cyclone predictions, reporting zero error on the landfall point and timing.A cyclone is an intense vortex or a whirl in the atmosphere with very strong winds circulating around it in an anti-clockwise direction in the Northern Hemisphere and in a clockwise direction in the Southern hemisphere. The word "Cyclone" is derived from the greek word “Cyclos" meaning the coil of a snake. Tropical cyclones are also referred to as 'Hurricanes' over Atlantic Ocean, 'Typhoons' over Pacific Ocean, 'Willy-Willies' over Australian Seas and simply as 'Cyclones' over north Indian ocean.On an average, out of five cyclones developing over the north Indian ocean (NIO) comprising bay of Bengal and Arabian sea annually, about three to four of them make landfall causing loss of life and property. Low - lying coastal belts of West Bengal, Odisha, Andhra Pradesh, Tamil Nadu and Puducherry are more prone to the impact of these systems.The number of deaths due to cyclones has, however, decreased significantly in the recent past, as a result of the improvement in the early warning capabilities of IMD.Get the latest India News and Live updates. articles.body: MUMBAI: A chilling audio purportedly featuring Anil Pandit, who claimed responsibility for the firing at actor Tiger Shroff’s car, has surfaced, with the speaker threatening Bollywood superstar Salman Khan and demanding an apology to jailed gangster Lawrence Bishnoi and the Bishnoi community.In the audio, shared by the Mumbai Crime Branch, Anil warned Salman Khan against relying on his security and threatened his family if he did not apologise.“Listen to me carefully, Salman Khan. If you don't apologise to my elder brother, Lawrence Bishnoi, or to the Bishnoi community, then we won't even leave a dog in your house. We will destroy your entire family. Keep this in mind. Don't think that you are in security and nothing will happen to you,” Anil Pandit said.The audio surfaced after three motorcycle-borne assailants allegedly opened fire at a BMW carrying Tiger Shroff in Mumbai’s Juhu area around 7pm on Sunday. The actor was leaving Pushpa Narsee Park, also known as Jamnabai Nursery, after attending a birthday gathering when the attackers fired multiple rounds at his vehicle.Two men allegedly opened fire while a third waited on a motorcycle to facilitate their escape. Seven rounds were reportedly fired. Shroff escaped without any gunshot injuries, although he sustained minor abrasions from shattered glass. His driver, Firdaus, suffered a bullet injury to his left hand, while a passerby was also injured.In a social media post, Pandit and another individual, Harman Sandhu, claimed responsibility for the attack, alleging that they had warned Shroff against working with Salman Khan but that he had ignored their warning.“Anyone in the Mumbai film industry who does not listen to us or works with Salman Khan will be next. Wait and watch,” the post read.The message also threatened rival groups allegedly using their name to gain notoriety. Police are verifying the authenticity of the social media post and the claims made in the audio.Mumbai Police have formed 15 teams, including personnel from the Crime Branch, to trace the assailants. articles.title: Dussehra 2026: 6 Simple things to buy on Vijayadashami for prosperity, positivity and new beginnings
articles.summary: When we talk about auspicious purchases on Dussehra, the first things that usually come to mind are gold, silver, vehicles or property.
articles.body: When we talk about auspicious purchases on Dussehra, the first things that usually come to mind are gold, silver, vehicles or property. But does every auspicious purchase have to be expensive?Not really.Vijayadashami celebrates the victory of good over evil, but it also marks an opportunity to make a fresh beginning. In many Indian families, buying something new on this day has been a tradition for generations.This year, the planetary positions make the occasion particularly interesting. The Sun is debilitated in Libra, Jupiter is exalted in Cancer, Mars is debilitated in Cancer, and Venus is retrograde in Libra. Saturn, meanwhile, continues its retrograde movement through Pisces.From an astrological perspective, these combinations bring attention to discipline, knowledge, relationships and everyday responsibilities.Here are six simple things I recommend purchasing this Dussehra.1. Copper Water Bottle: For Sun Energy and DisciplineThe Sun represents vitality, authority, confidence and discipline in astrology. With the Sun debilitated in Libra during Vijayadashami, a copper water bottle makes an interesting symbolic purchase.Rather than keeping it only for decorative purposes, make it part of your daily routine. The idea is to associate the purchase with better habits and greater consistency.Copper has a traditional association with Surya Dev, although drinking from copper vessels does not scientifically strengthen the Sun. Use a food-safe bottle and follow its care instructions.2. New Diary and Pen: For Knowledge and Career GrowthHow many plans have you made this year that are still waiting to be implemented?With Jupiter exalted in Cancer and Mercury influencing Libra, this Vijayadashami is a meaningful occasion to purchase a new diary and pen.I particularly recommend this for students, researchers, entrepreneurs and working professionals.Write down three things you genuinely want to accomplish before the year ends. They could relate to your career, education, finances or personal development.3. Green Indoor Plant: For Growth and Fresh EnergyA small green plant can be a wonderful addition to your home or workplace.Mercury is associated with green, communication, learning and business intelligence. From a Vastu and astrological perspective, bringing a healthy plant home can symbolise growth and renewal.You can choose a money plant, jade plant or another easy-to-maintain indoor variety.Place it somewhere it receives suitable light and regular care. A neglected plant defeats the very purpose of bringing something living into your surroundings.4. Wooden Desk Organiser: For Stability and Better Work HabitsThis will sound like an unusual Dussehra purchase, but think about your working desk for a moment.How many old bills, unused pens, visiting cards and unfinished documents are lying around?With Saturn retrograde in Pisces, I would particularly recommend bringing some order to your professional surroundings.Purchase a simple wooden desk organiser and use Vijayadashami to clear unnecessary clutter.In traditional symbolism, wood represents growth and natural stability, while Saturn is associated with discipline and responsibility.Sometimes, the fresh beginning we need is simply a better-organised workplace.5. Comfortable Walking Shoes: For Mars Energy and Physical DisciplineWe often associate auspicious purchases with objects kept inside the house. But why not buy something that encourages you to take better care of yourself?Mars, the planet associated with physical energy, courage and action, is debilitated in Cancer during this period.A comfortable pair of walking shoes can become a practical reminder to pay attention to physical activity.You don't need an expensive brand. Choose something that fits properly and suits your walking routine.If you have been postponing your morning walks or regular exercise, let Vijayadashami become the day you decide to begin.6. New Clothes for Children or Parents: For Family BlessingsOf all six purchases, this is perhaps the one I would recommend most strongly.Instead of buying something for yourself, consider purchasing new clothes for your parents or children.Jupiter's exalted position in Cancer draws attention, in traditional astrological interpretation, to family values, nourishment and blessings. Venus, meanwhile, represents clothing, comfort and affection.Buying clothes for your parents can be a gesture of gratitude. Purchasing something for children brings its own happiness, particularly during the festive season.And there is no need to make it expensive.A simple kurta, saree, shirt or festive outfit chosen with affection can carry far more personal meaning than a costly purchase made without thought.Get the latest astrology news and horoscope updates. articles.title: Texas landowners challenge $46 billion border wall as separate lawsuit halts construction in Big Bend
articles.summary: A $46 billion plan to expand the US-Mexico border wall is facing resistance from Texas landowners, while a separate lawsuit has halted construction in the
articles.body: A $46 billion plan to expand the US-Mexico border wall is facing resistance from Texas landowners, while a separate lawsuit has halted construction in the Big Bend region. On October 2, 2026, US District Judge Kathleen Cardone of the Western District of Texas, in El Paso, granted a preliminary injunction in a case brought by the Center for Biological Diversity, Friends of the Ruidosa Church and river guide Danny Miller Jr. The order blocks specified construction activities while the case proceeds and stays the federal waivers used to expedite the project. Separately, the No Big Bend Wall Coalition, which says its network includes more than 200 landowners, has challenged the administration’s plans. The disputes concern federal authority, private property, environmental protections and the need for border barriers in a region with comparatively few Border Patrol arrests.Big Bend border wall project: $7.5 billion plan and why Texas is differentThe $46 billion figure comes from funding approved by Republicans in 2025 as part of a broader immigration enforcement package, according to Associated Press reporting published by ABC News. The administration’s plan covers the roughly 2,000-mile US-Mexico border and includes walls, vehicle barriers, patrol roads and surveillance technology. The first border wall panels in the Big Bend region went up in mid-September 2026, although ground-disturbing work in Big Bend National Park had been documented as early as August. The administration plans to spend $7.5 billion to strengthen border infrastructure along a stretch of more than 500 miles. The region accounts for roughly one-quarter of the entire US-Mexico border, but its geography differs from that of more heavily developed border areas.Parts of the Rio Grande run below steep limestone cliffs, while remote stretches are accessible only by rocky trails and through difficult desert terrain. Supporters of the project argue that walls, vehicle barriers, patrol roads and surveillance technology are needed to deter crossings and smuggling. The administration has also warned that leaving gaps in border infrastructure could push illegal crossings and smuggling toward less fortified areas. Border Patrol arrest figures cited by AP illustrate the difference in enforcement activity across the region. In August 2026, agents arrested 8,870 people along the entire southern border, including 161 in the Big Bend sector. These figures measure arrests, not the total number of attempted crossings. Opponents argue that the region’s natural barriers and comparatively low number of arrests make an extensive wall unnecessary. Some local law enforcement officials have advocated surveillance towers and drones as alternatives. Customs and Border Protection has said it is building an average of about 12 miles of barrier per week and recently passed 200 miles of new barriers built during President Donald Trump’s second term, according to AP. The administration says the infrastructure is part of its wider effort to maintain low levels of illegal border crossings.Texas landowners’ border wall lawsuit: eminent domain and the construction pauseTexas presents a particular challenge for federal construction because much of the land along the border is privately or state-owned. The government must obtain authorisation to enter private property for surveys and construction. When owners refuse access, federal authorities can pursue eminent domain, the process through which the government takes private property for public use in exchange for compensation. According to AP reporting on the legal disputes, courts have generally deferred to the government in eminent domain cases, and earlier lawsuits seeking to stop border wall projects have largely failed. A Justice Department official who spoke to AP on condition of anonymity said the Customs and Border Protection had reached agreements with dozens of Big Bend landowners. Across the southern border, about 70 cases had been referred to the department during Trump’s second term, with 50 resolved and none requiring a trial, the official said.The No Big Bend Wall Coalition has separately challenged the project, arguing that the Department of Homeland Security is misusing its authority in a region with limited illegal cross-border activity. The coalition’s lawsuit is distinct from the case that produced the October 2 injunction. That injunction was granted by US District Judge Kathleen Cardone in a lawsuit brought by the Center for Biological Diversity, Friends of the Ruidosa Church and Big Bend river guide and landowner Danny Miller Jr. The plaintiffs challenged the federal government’s use of waivers to bypass environmental and other laws to accelerate construction. The preliminary injunction covers the Big Bend Border Patrol Sector within one mile of the Rio Grande, as well as Big Bend National Park and Big Bend Ranch State Park. It also stays the relevant federal waivers while the case proceeds. The order remains in effect until the court resolves the case on its merits, unless it is modified or stayed. As of October 15, 2026, the Trump administration was seeking to suspend the injunction while pursuing Supreme Court review. In a court filing reported by Marfa Public Radio on October 9, the government asked Judge Cardone to suspend the order and said it intended to seek relief from the Supreme Court. Inside Climate News reported on October 15 that Justice Department attorneys were continuing to pursue that course.Big Bend landowners and local officials oppose constructionResistance extends beyond the courtroom. Landowners and business owners have attended county meetings, protested against proposed agreements with contractors and monitored construction areas for possible violations. Some have urged local authorities not to provide land or road access to companies working on the project. In Terrell County, residents unsuccessfully opposed leasing airport land to a barrier contractor. In Jeff Davis County, a proposed agreement allowing another contractor to use a county road had not been approved at the time of AP’s reporting. Terrell County Judge Dale Lynn Carruthers said the county had limited control over the federal project and suggested that refusing the lease might simply lead the contractor to find another location.Opposition has also come from some Republicans. Rancher Laura Allen, who said she voted for Trump twice, supports securing the border but believes spending billions on barriers in Big Bend is unnecessary. Terrell County Sheriff Thad Cleveland, a former Border Patrol agent, has argued that drones and surveillance towers are more suitable for the rugged terrain he patrols. Republican Sen. John Cornyn has pressed the Department of Homeland Security about Texans’ concerns following bulldozing in Big Bend National Park. Local opponents have raised concerns about the effects of construction on tourism, access to the Rio Grande and ranching operations. Some residents and property owners have also expressed concern about the consequences for the region’s natural environment.The Zuberbueler family, whose Val Verde County ranch dates to 1898, is concerned about the effect of construction on livestock and water supplies. The family raises Angora goats and Rambouillet sheep on land extending toward the Rio Grande. Although the animals can pass through vehicle barriers, the family says the barriers could prevent cowboys from moving freely across the property. Earlier border wall disputes provide historical context for the use of eminent domain. A 2017 ProPublica investigation reported that the Department of Homeland Security filed more than 360 eminent domain lawsuits in less than a year after 2007 across Texas, New Mexico, Arizona and California. Some landowners remained involved in court proceedings for years. The immediate future of the Big Bend project depends in part on the ongoing legal proceedings. The temporary order has halted construction while the administration challenges it, but it does not by itself resolve the broader dispute over federal authority, property access or the merits of building a wall across the region. The court proceedings will determine how the legal challenge proceeds as landowners and officials continue to contest the project.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.
